narrative:
Lifecycle events move about USD 1.9B of rare disease revenue in FY2026. Soliris faces biosimilar erosion in the US and Europe (down from USD 960M to USD 720M across PNH and gMG in the two markets), while Ultomiris PNH in Europe grows as patients convert.

Voydeya, the add-on for extravascular haemolysis in PNH, more than doubles from a small base. Koselugo grows across the US, Europe and China as the adult NF1-PN label lets ageing-out paediatric patients stay on therapy.

The key judgement is erosion speed. European tender data shows biosimilar switching below the early forecast, which argues for a slower Soliris erosion curve.
